info.title: Porthole implemented HTTP API
info.description: Implemented OTLP intake, bounded telemetry queries, configuration definitions and dashboards. Native session security uses the installation session cookie; development cookie names vary by local origin. All requests remain subject to configured origin checks and current scope. This document contains no installation settings. It does not advertise complete vendor language or transport compatibility.

post.description: OTLP over HTTP, version 1.9.0. Accepts JSON or protobuf with identity or gzip encoding. Success records durable acceptance, not completed processing. Each resource needs service, environment and team within the credential grants; missing dimensions inherit only a single explicit grant. Resource attributes take precedence over scope headers. Empty export objects are supported. No raw gRPC transport.

post.description: No URL query parameters. Requires telemetry.read on a bearer credential, or a native session. Native POST requests require a same-origin Origin header. Full vendor query languages are not supported.

400.description: Correct the rejected input; expression errors include field and hint when available.

401.description: Sign in or supply a valid live credential.

403.description: Use an authorized scope and action. Native writes require the configured same-origin Origin header.

404.description: Check the identifier and current access; inaccessible objects may be hidden.

409.description: Refresh current authority and revision; reuse an idempotency key only for the identical request.

415.description: Use a supported Content-Type and encoding.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait

503.description: Restore service availability and retry; a failed request is not evidence of acceptance.

Idempotency-Key is optional and makes repeated identical native writes durable. Native writes require owner, admin or maintainer role and a same-origin Origin header. JSON bodies are limited to 8192 bytes.

409.description: Refresh current authority and revision; reuse an idempotency key only for the identical request.

503.description: Restore service availability and retry; a failed request is not evidence of acceptance.

ScopedCredential.description: Porthole scoped credential in Authorization. Intake requires telemetry.write; queries require telemetry.read; definition reads require definitions.read. Signal and resource grants, live custody and limits apply. Credentials in URL query parameters are forbidden.

NativeSession.name: __Host-operator_session
NativeSession.description: Native installation session. Local development uses an origin-specific cookie name. Native mutation roles are owner, admin or maintainer; unsafe requests require a same-origin Origin header. Authorization credentials cannot mutate definitions.

QueryInput.description: JSON object, at most 8192 bytes; duplicate keys refuse. Visual queries need signal. Text dialects can infer signal. Native scope filters are optional and intersect live grants. Empty optional fields mean unset. Native and expression filters must agree.

expression.description: Visual requires empty text. PromQL supports one bare metric selector with exact scope labels. SQL supports COUNT(*) on logs, AVG(value) on metrics with one exact metric, or discrete p95 duration on traces, with exact scope equalities. Lucene supports exact log scope terms joined by AND. No general query-language execution; unsupported syntax refuses.

from.description: Inclusive unsigned 64-bit Unix nanoseconds. Use decimal strings to avoid numeric precision loss.

through.description: Inclusive Unix nanoseconds, at least from.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor returned by a previous page.

snapshot.description: Nonnegative safe integer completion watermark; defaults to latest completed batch.

limit.description: Integer 1 to 200, or up to 2000 when trace is selected. Default 100.

metric.description: Exact metric name, metrics only; control characters refuse.

items.description: Retained normalized telemetry row with object payload; shape depends on signal and storage backend.

aggregate.description: Aggregate is null when pagination makes the result partial, and for empty numeric selections. Count is zero on a complete empty result.
